title: Silly String: Disaster in a Can
summary: Josh and Chuck cover Silly String, the aerosol string-foam toy. They trace its origin to a 1972 patent by inventor Leonard A. Fish and chemist Robert Cox, who were developing a spray-on emergency cast, and its licensing to Wham-O after a demonstration. They correct the myth that Julius Simon invented it: Simon's company Just for Kicks later bought the rights around 1999-era marketing (about thirty years later). They explain the ingredients (resin, surfactant such as Tween 85, propellant, talc, solvent, ammonia and alcohol stabilizers), the historical use of Freon-12 and its replacement with HFCs and their global warming potential, the freezing-can hazard, the military use of Silly String to detect trip wires, a 2007 New Jersey mother's collection of Silly String for troops, and a Los Angeles Hollywood Halloween ban with its fine. Ends with listener mail thanking the hosts and praising the ad jingles.
topics: Los Angeles Halloween silly string ban

segments.title: Intro and history of Silly String
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the episode, describe what Silly String is, and recount its origin: a 1972 patent by Leonard Fish and Robert Cox for a spray-on emergency cast, its pitch to Wham-O, and Julius Simon's later connection through Just for Kicks and Car Freshener Corporation.

segments.title: Silly String ingredients and chemistry
segments.summary: The hosts explain the balance of adhesiveness and cohesiveness, the roles of resin, propellant, surfactant, talc, solvent, and stabilizers, and that Freon-12 was once used but has been replaced.

segments.title: Sponsor break and banter
segments.summary: A break in the program with banter about the hosts' camera and older episodes that embedded an ad.

segments.title: Military use, environment, and freezing cans
segments.summary: The hosts describe the US military's use of Silly String to spot trip wires, a 2007 New Jersey mother's collection for troops, HFC replacements and their global warming potential, warnings about flammability, and cans freezing skin.

segments.title: Los Angeles Halloween ban
segments.summary: Council member Tom LaBonge's push in the mid-2000s to ban Silly String in Los Angeles on Halloween due to cleanup costs, with the fine for possession described.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts read listener mail from Amy in Agoura Hills, California, praising the show and the listener-submitted ad jingles, and give the contact address.
